To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a novel HiPIP:oxygen reductase has been identified in a thermohalophillic bacterium; (2) this oxidase is a caa-type, with haems of the As type and a low potential; (3) the subunit I of the caa3 oxidases of this bacterium and of the COX-type enzymes are similar; (4) a major difference is the lack of the glutamate residue in the D-channel of the R.
the R. marinis oxidase is the first example of an enzyme that uses HiPIP as electron donor and that it has a novel proton uptake pathway, which is different from that of other oxidases.
a HiPIP:o oxygen oxidoreductase has been isolated and characterized and the first enzyme lacking the key glutamic acid of the D channel has been identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the structure and function of respiratory enzymes of the thermohalic bacterium Rhodotermus marinus, a bacterium which grows at high temperatures, high salt concentrations and low pH values.
the discovery and characterisation of a novel HiPIP:oxygen terminal oxidase, which has a novel haem A3 and lacks the glutamate of the proton channel.

the elucidation of the structure and function of an enzyme that has a novel combination of structural features, which may be of general importance to the understanding of the mechanisms of the respiratory chains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the R. marinis caa3 oxidases are not COX-type, but that they share a common ancestor.
the D-channel of the R. marinusb caa3 oxidases lacks the key glutamate, which may be substituted by a tyrosine.
R. marinus is a new model for the study of the mechanism of proton pumping and for the study of proton channels in biological systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the respiratory chain of R. marimus has a caa3 oxidoreductase that is a HiPIP:o2 oxidoreductase and that, in this oxidase, tyrosine is a possible substitute for the key glutamate in the D-channel.
the R. marinis caa3 oxidases are the first example of HiPIP:oxygen reductases, and the only known example of a HiPPO lacking the key glutamates of the D-channel.
R. marinus is an interesting model for studying the evolution of the terminal oxidase superfamily.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the R. marinis oxidase is the first example of HiPIP:oxygen-oxidoreductase and the first example of caa3 oxidases lacking the glutamate of the proton channel.

the caa3 terminal quinol oxidase of Rhodothermus marinussubunit I is the first example of an enzyme lacking the essential glutamate in the D-channel, and that tyrosine may substitute the role of this residue in the proton pumping mechanism.
the D-channel is not an essential feature in proton pumping oxidases.
